title: Integration tests for a social feed query
name: Social feed query tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these integration tests set up data and assert on the results? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does the pagination test pass the last item's createdAt rather than an offset to fetch the second page?
choices: Offsets are not supported by Postgres with ORDER BY
The cursor filters on created_at < cursor, so the second page starts strictly after the last item seen and stays stable if newer posts are inserted between calls
It makes the query use fewer bind parameters
An offset would return the pages in ascending order

questions.prompt: Why does seedUser append part of a UUID to each handle?
choices: It makes the feed sort deterministic
So a unique constraint on handle cannot collide if rows from another test or a parallel run are still present
To bypass the follows foreign key

questions.prompt: In the first test, what does seeding a deleted post with the newest timestamp verify that a deleted post with the oldest timestamp would not?
choices: That the deleted_at filter is applied before LIMIT, since the deleted post would otherwise be first in the result
That the JOIN on follows is correct
That posts from unfollowed users are hidden
Nothing; both positions test the same thing equally
